Synthetic samples with a known price elasticity

Source: R/elasticity.R
simulate_elasticity_sample.Rd

Builds one of four daily samples. The first two are a single series. The segment samples have one resident row and one visitor row per date. aggregate_segment_rounds() turns those rows into a daily total and a round-weighted average price.

Usage

simulate_elasticity_sample(
  experiment = c("correct_specification", "endogenous_price", "segment_mix",
    "segment_mix_price_variation"),
  n_days = 400,
  elasticity = -0.8,
  seed = 457
)

Arguments

experiment

One of correct_specification, endogenous_price, segment_mix, or segment_mix_price_variation.

n_days

Number of dates.

elasticity

Structural price coefficient. Ignored when experiment is segment_mix, because those prices do not vary and the rounds are not generated from a price term.

seed

Integer seed. The generator restores the previous random seed when it finishes.

Value

A golfops_elasticity_sample tibble. Attributes description and dgp state the experiment and the generating equation.

Details

correct_specification draws price independently of the demand shock and generates log rounds from elasticity, weekend, temperature, and precipitation. endogenous_price raises price when anticipated demand is higher. Part of that demand is the weekend and the temperature, and part is not returned in the table. segment_mix keeps each segment price constant and shifts the visitor share by season. The elasticity argument is not used to generate those rounds. segment_mix_price_variation gives both segments the same negative elasticity and modest price noise that is independent of the demand shock, while the visitor share still shifts.

These rows are synthetic. They are not Dobson Ranch, and they are not the Enz and Canina transaction file.

Examples

simulate_elasticity_sample("correct_specification", n_days = 40, seed = 457)
#> Price is drawn independently of the demand shock. Log rounds use the stated elasticity plus weekend, temperature, and precipitation.
